run_note: Run covering 2026-08-12 -> 2026-08-13, executed 12:35 UTC Thursday, US pre-market (08:35 ET). NO R1 BREACH (weakest book is hunter at 973.38, 223.38 above the 750 line) and NO SIM-INTEGRITY ALERT - but the alert check passed VACUOUSLY, not cleanly: all nine trades[] arrays are byte-identical to the 2026-08-12 supervisor commit, so the fleet placed ZERO fills in 24h and there was nothing to audit. STALENESS CHECK CLEAN: all nine states last_updated within 11.5-11.7 minutes, tightly clustered, no freeze-guard misfire. THE HEADLINE IS UPTIME. Two blackouts in the last 24h - 08-12 13:04:58Z -> 19:14:44Z (6h09m) and 08-13 00:49:41Z -> 06:57:40Z (5h55m) - left the fleet dark 12h04m, ~50% of wall-clock, for a SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY against the workflow's own documented 82% design target. I now have the mechanism at job-level granularity rather than by inference. The trading loop is one job capped at 345 minutes; when it ends, the fleet is dead until GitHub both CREATES a new scheduled run and DISPATCHES its job, and both legs failed. Run 31616014589 was created 08-12 16:07:39Z but its job was not created until 19:13:20Z - 3h06m of pure dispatch queueing - then ran its full loop to 01:02:42Z. After that loop ended, GitHub created NO trading-loop run at all for 4h15m (the 00:49 and 05:10 runs are short auxiliary jobs, 20-60s each), and when run 31669845931 was finally created at 05:17:53Z its job waited a further 1h40m to start at 06:57:40Z. So the 6h holes are not one fault but two stacked ones: dropped cron creation plus multi-hour dispatch queueing, on top of a loop that cannot span more than 6h by GitHub's own job cap. The workflow comment already measured 6% cron acceptance and sized the loop for it; what is new is that the mitigation is delivering 50% coverage, not the 82% it was designed for, two days running. THIS IS THE ESCALATION CONDITION - an external trigger is the only fix inside the owner's control. COST IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the first hole covered 09:04-15:14 ET, roughly 88% of the 08-12 US regular session, the second consecutive session lost this way after 08-11's 09:34-15:43 ET hole. Seven equity books could not evaluate a signal for nearly two full sessions, and the fleet's zero-trade day should be read against that, not as calm. THE GROK WATCHER IS DARK 146 HOURS and its damage is now PROVEN rather than inferred: data/sentinel_state.json's newest scan is still 2026-08-07T10:47:38Z and its hype list still contains NET, so the hype bot's exit condition ('NET drops off the euphoric list') can never evaluate true - it is day six of a 1-2 day strategy with no stop. The risk gate itself behaves correctly, printing 'WATCHER STALE ... treat risk as UNKNOWN' every cycle. NEW ANALYST DEFECT, worse than yesterday's misquote: in its 08-11 decision it asserted 'Watcher remains caution, not SEVERE' while its own tools_called list contains only get_price_history - it reported a tool-derived fact it never fetched, about a source dark 96 hours at the time. CONGRESS STALE-MARK FAULT FROM 08-12 IS RESOLVED: all four legs reconcile to 1,012.85 vs 1,012.84 published.
